market_commentary:
Canadian equities led a broad advance in the week ending April 10 — the S&P/TSX Composite climbed 5.51% to 33,696, extending its 12-month gain to 42.85%1, while the S&P 500 added 3.6% to 6,816.892. WTI crude eased to ~US$98/bbl from US$102.18 on March 313, and the Canadian dollar held at 0.7200 CAD/USD (USD/CAD 1.3832) as the Bank of Canada maintained its policy rate at 2.25% for a seventh meeting4. The Signal Dispatch database tracks 7,427 capital projects valued at $1,472 billion5.

Rate-sensitive sectors dominate the pipeline cross-reference — the database contains 970 residential, commercial, and infrastructure projects totalling $325 billion with financing exposure to the Government of Canada curve, which traded at 2.79% at the 2-year and 3.46% at the 10-year for a 67 basis point spread6. The 150 mining projects ($168 billion) carry revenue exposure as copper rose 3.9% to US$5.87/lb and silver added 1.91% to US$76.32/oz7. If WTI holds near US$98, the 42 oil and gas projects ($100.5 billion) linked to crude pricing would see a fourth week below the end-March US$102 peak3.
